chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us said: Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Ash'ari narrated to us, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboob, from Habib al-Sajistani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:

Friday is a day of worship, so worship God, the Mighty and Majestic. Saturday is for the Household of Muhammad (peace be upon them). Sunday is for their followers. Monday is the day of the Umayyads. Tuesday is a day of ease. Wednesday is for the Abbasids and their victory. Thursday is a blessed day; its dawn is blessed for my Ummah.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and historical significance of each day of the week in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* presents a unique cosmological and historical framework where each day of the week is spiritually aligned with specific dynasties or communities, reflecting the Shia perspective on Islamic history. While Friday remains the universal day of worship, the assignment of Saturday to the Ahl al-Bayt and Sunday to their followers underscores the centrality of the Imams in Shia eschatology, whereas Monday’s link to the Umayyads and Wednesday to the Abbasids highlights the transient nature of political power. The designation of Thursday as a blessed day for the Ummah serves as a reminder of divine favor and the culmination of the week’s spiritual cycle.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-60 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Ali ibn Abdullah ibn Ishaq al-Ash’ari, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Mahboob, on the authority of Habib al-Sejestani, on the authority of Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) that God’s Prophet (MGB) said,

“Fridays are days of worship. Thus, worship the Honorable the Exalted God. Saturdays are for the members of the Holy Household. Sundays are for their followers. Mondays are for the Umayyads. Tuesdays are easy days. Wednesdays are for the Abbasids and their victory. Thursdays are blessed days. For my followers its dawn is blessed.”
